audit.why: A tank mirror where nobody dies, with Cho'Gath owning the Vorpal Spikes and Feral Scream window at 4-5 and the Feast scaling late, and Sejuani owning level 2-3 and level 6. The entry's stage sides say this and the 48.89 win rate supports a near-even lane. Neither chart needed moving.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and spikes[3].text both claim that two tank items stop Feast: 'Feast true damage cannot execute through Sunfire Aegis plus a second tank item' and 'even Feast true damage can't chunk through two full tank items fast enough'.
audit.why: Feast is true damage on a percentage of maximum health. Riot's text: 'Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage.' Armour and magic resist do nothing against it, and stacking maximum health makes the percentage component larger, not smaller — so the entry's late-game reassurance is not merely optimistic, it is inverted, and it is aimed squarely at the champion whose entire item path is health and resistances. A Sejuani who believes two tank items make her immune to Feast will stand in exactly the spot where it kills her. late gets this right ('the one tool that punches through your armor stacking'), so the entry contradicts itself.
audit.corrected: whys[6] and spikes[3].text now state that Feast ignores armour and that the answer is playing around its 80-second cooldown, matching what late already said.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream's silence is correctly identified as the counter to Permafrost, but neither its 300 range nor its 11s cooldown is ever given. 'Vorpal Spines' is used for Vorpal Spikes in whys[3], spikes[2].text and early. Rupture's cooldown is never stated anywhere.
audit.why: Feral Scream reaching only 300 units is the whole counterplay and it is missing: Sejuani's Winter's Wrath is 600 and Permafrost is 560, so both of her abilities outrange the silence, and 'respect the silence range' becomes an actual instruction once the number is attached. Vorpal Spikes is Riot's name; Spines is not an ability. And Rupture at 6 seconds flat at every rank is the most important omission in the entry, for the reason below.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream's 300 range and 11s cooldown are now in spikes[2].text, wants.foe[1], mid and breakdown.cooldowns. Vorpal Spikes is spelled correctly in whys[3], spikes[2].text and early. Rupture's 6s is in early, mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid tells the reader to 'step up only when you see Rupture on cooldown', and breakdown.cooldowns builds the whole green-light system on Rupture being down.
audit.why: Rupture is 6 seconds flat at every rank — the shortest cooldown in either kit apart from Permafrost itself. It is never meaningfully down, so an entry that gates every step-up on its cooldown is gating them on a condition that will not arrive, and the reader either never steps up or learns to ignore the advice. The cooldown that can actually be played around is Feral Scream at 11 seconds, which is also the one that stops the stun. Rupture's counterplay is spatial, not temporal: it is a telegraphed ground cast and the entry already tells the reader to sidestep it, which is correct and sufficient.
audit.corrected: early, mid and breakdown.cooldowns now say Rupture is 6s flat and cannot be waited out, and repoint the trade window to Feral Scream's 11s.

edits.after: At Level 1 neither of you has meaningful damage — take W, hit the wave, and give nothing. His Rupture (Q) is the only threat: a slow-moving ground AoE that telegraphs clearly, so step laterally the moment the crack appears and you dodge it free. Note the cooldown before you plan around it — Rupture is 6 seconds flat at every rank, so it is never really down and sidestepping is the only counterplay. At Level 2 your Q changes the equation: step up when he is walking toward a minion and land the Arctic Assault knock-up before he can place the crack under you. At Level 3 you have the full chain — Q to knock him up, both Winter's Wrath arcs to fill the Frost gauge, then Permafrost to stun. Just respect the Vorpal Spikes chip on the walk-out.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Cho'Gath's window: Vorpal Spikes procs on every hit, Feral Scream is long enough to cancel your Permafrost if he lands it first, and his HP pool compounds. Do not plan a trade around Rupture being down — it is 6 seconds flat at every rank. Plan around Feral Scream instead: it is 11 seconds at rank 1 and reaches only 300 units, so fight from outside it, fill the gauge with a W double-arc, stun, and walk before it comes back. At Level 6 the lane swings back: Glacial Prison reaches 1300 units, far past anything he can answer, and guarantees a stun into your chain. Fire it as he steps past the halfway point, Permafrost while he is locked, and walk through him with both W arcs. He has no mobility and no answer to a clean R.

At Level 6 the lane swings decisively back: Glacial Prison outranges Rupture, travels faster than he can dodge at melee range, and guarantees a full stun into E chain. edits.after: - Cho'Gath Rupture: 6 seconds flat at every rank — it is never really down, so sidestep it rather than waiting it out. - Feral Scream: 11s at rank 1, 300 range, and it eats your E. - Feast: 80s at rank 1, true damage.
edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture (Knockup): matchup-defining — Telegraphed knockup — sidestep it and he has no engage at all. Check it before every step-up. - Q dash is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

notes:
The single most useful fact in this matchup was inverted in two fields: two tank items do not protect you from Feast. It is true damage scaling on a percentage of max health, so a Sejuani building health and resistances gets less protection from her items here than almost anyone, not more. late already said this correctly, which means the entry was arguing with itself.

The second was a green-light system built on a 6-second cooldown. Same failure mode as the Ambessa entry, which gated everything on Permafrost's 1.5s cooldown — worth checking whether a generator is emitting 'fight when X is down' lines without consulting the cooldown field, because that would explain both.

'Vorpal Spines' for Vorpal Spikes, three occurrences, now correct. This one the packet's suspectNames check did catch.

The full layer writes his Q as 'Rupture (Knockup)' in winCon, enemyWin and loading. Harmless but non-standard; a reader looking for 'Rupture (Knockup)' in his ability list will not find it. Not fixed — the parenthetical is 10 characters and removing it breaks the band on all three.
